title: The Benchmarks Game: Why It's Rigged and How You Can (Really) Win - Darius Emrani
talk_summary: Darius Emrani argues public AI benchmarks are gamed via unequal configurations, privileged test-set access, and style-over-substance optimization, so leaderboard scores are unreliable for choosing models. He recommends building private, production-derived evals with chosen metrics (quality/cost/latency), testing candidate models on your own data, and running them continuously in a pre-deployment loop.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of academic/leaderboard questions, they sample real queries from the production system and use those as the test set, because real user problems are more predictive than synthetic benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Taking five actual queries from your production system is worth way way more than 100 academic questions.

takeaways.technique: Test top-N models on your own data, not leaderboards
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly ignore leaderboard rankings and instead run the top ~5 candidate models against their own domain data, since a model that tops generic benchmarks can fail on your documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Test the top five models on your specific data. GPT4 might top generic benchmarks, but fail on your legal documents.

takeaways.what_they_do: They pick metrics per application rather than a single accuracy number, explicitly including cost and latency alongside quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Quality, cost, latency. Pick what matters for your application.

takeaways.what_they_do: They systematize evals into a repeatable cycle: identify issues, build improvements, run evals before deploy, only deploy when hitting the quality bar, then monitor and repeat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You run evals, you get feedback, you improve, and then you only deploy when you hit your quality bar

takeaways.technique: Control for style/length effects in LLM judging
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite that filtering out style effects (length, formatting, personality) completely reorders rankings, because judges reward charm over correctness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When they filtered out style effects, length, formatting, personality, the rankings completely changed.
takeaways.numbers: 39% of SAT score variance is essay length (cited)

takeaways.technique: Rotate test questions to prevent overfitting
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend regularly rotating test-set questions so models/prompts can't overfit to a fixed eval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to have regular rotation of the test questions to prevent overfitting
